[agent-bulk] Verdict shower 24112 (546.3 MeV, pdg 11, 23 seg, 104.6 cm) = highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; the only higher-kine_charge thing I passed over is 24114 (pdg 211, kine_charge 118.7 / kine_best 55.6). Vertex judged from the automatic close-in vtxz-* frames (r95 160.7 cm, half_span 200.8, so vtxz fired): the star sits at the convergence of a 152 cm straight track and the shower stem in both vtxz-az-055-el+20 and vtxz-az+065-el+20 -- the vertex is fine, this is not a vertex verdict. OVER-CLUSTERED, and the defect is at the start: 24112's seed is segment 24112, a 1.9 cm stub in cluster 24, attached by site 'stem_backfill (direct)'. Cluster 24 is the vertex TRACK cluster -- it also holds 24111 (pdg 13, 151.9 cm, unowned/grey), 24113 (pdg 211, 23.2 cm, unowned/grey), 24114 and 24115. So the reconstruction anchored a 546 MeV EM shower on a stub of the muon/pion stem cluster, and the shower's reco start comes out at (97.6, 118.7, 278.9), which is the main vertex to 0.1 cm. That is the brief's 'swallows a straight minimum-ionising stem' case. start/axis wrong: the real body of this shower is cluster 107 (7 segments, 11.5-27.1 cm, 1.5-13.3 deg off axis) plus clusters 90/91/93/97/108/119 out to 113 cm -- there is a ~10 cm gap between the 1.9 cm vertex stub and the next member, and the charge in that gap belongs to the unowned muon 24111 and pion 24113. It also absorbed 97031 (pdg 2212, 1.3 cm) at 35.1 cm / 13.4 deg by pass4_angle. Mark: segment 24112 OUT of shower 24112. That mark is WEAK in charge (1.9 cm of a 546 MeV object, it will not move the energy) but it is the whole structural claim -- it is the piece that puts the start on the vertex; if the owner reads the conversion as genuinely happening within ~2 cm of the vertex (possible for a photon, just improbable) the mark reverses and the verdict with it, which is why this is 'likely' and not 'certain'. PI0 -- this is another instance of the wave-2 pattern, and I priced the alternatives with --pio-pairs. The reco accepted group 0 = 24112 + 31010, stored mass 110.5 MeV. It is implausible twice over: (a) gamma1 = 24112 starts EXACTLY on the neutrino vertex, so it cannot be a converted photon and the display's vertex convention has no chord at all ('theta - -> m = -'), only the axis convention exists, which is exactly the wave-2 finding; (b) gamma2 = 31010 starts at (-32.7, 43.9, 395.1), 190.0 cm from the vertex and on the far side of x=0, i.e. a 50 MeV photon that flew 190 cm before converting. Priced alternatives (axis convention / vertex convention): 24112+31010 (the reco's own) 79.2 / -- , note the display's own axis number 79.2 does not even agree with the reco's stored 110.5; 24112+106049 132.8 [in the accept window] / -- ; 106049+31010 8.7 / 3.5 ; 106049+117107 55.4 / 3.1. The best-priced pairing is 24112 + 106049 at 132.8 MeV, 2 MeV off the pi0 mass, and it is also what kine_pio_* points at (137.0 + 546.3 at 25.7 deg) -- 106049 (137.0 MeV, 5 seg, 34.5 cm) starts at (52.8, 96.0, 317.1), a clean 63.1 cm detached from the vertex, the most photon-like object in the event. I have STORED 24112+106049 as a candidate, NOT as a settled answer: it inherits gamma1's vertex-anchored start, so its vertex convention is also empty, and if my over-clustering call is right the true gamma1 is the cluster-107 body starting ~11.5 cm out, which is not a separate reco shower and therefore cannot be slotted at all. That is the honest reading: the pairing cannot be fixed without first fixing the start. Showers I did not open frames for: 31010, 117107, 94028, 102032, 24114, 24115 (I used their table numbers only); 11 of the 19 showers are below the 20 MeV scope threshold and were never drawn. This verdict is about clustering and is silent on PID. Images looked at: 6.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, and the cleanest event in my shard. Verdict shower 11009 (468.4 MeV, pdg 11, 22 seg, 124.5 cm) is the ONLY shower in scope -- it is trivially the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object and there is no higher-energy non-EM object to pass over. Vertex judged from the automatic close-in vtxz-* frames (r95 360.6 cm, so the vtx-* set is +-400 cm and unusable): in both vtxz-az-055-el+20 and vtxz-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly at the tip of a single narrow MIP-like stem that broadens into a shower ~40 cm downstream -- one prong, no second prong, no ambiguity. That is the textbook nue CC picture and the shower start X sits on the star, which is correct for an electron (not a photon gap). CORRECT: the yellow member set covers the whole visible point cloud from the stem tip through the shower body, single apex, and the acceptance plot shows only orange squares -- there is not a single non-member candidate inside the plotted range. Non-members do exist but are irrelevant: 35026 at 24.1 cm / 40.3 deg (0.4 cm) and 36027 at 38.8 cm / 61.4 deg (0.3 cm), both sub-cm stubs at wide angle and off the top of the acceptance plot; everything else in the event is 222-388 cm away. There is NO grey/unowned charge anywhere in this event -- every segment has an owner -- so the strong under-clustering case cannot arise here. Membership triple-check: nseg 22 = owner-grouped count 22 = cmp_div's 22. 'Correct' here is a fast pass in the pilot's sense: nothing jumped out at four cameras and the candidate table, not a segment-by-segment verification. The one thing I would flag for a second eye is the reach -- 11009 claims pieces out to 104.7 cm (46039/46040/46041, 37028, 38029, 39030) at 3-11 deg, i.e. tier-2 pass3_cone pickups ~7 radiation lengths downstream, and it also absorbed 45034 and 38029 (pdg 2212) and four pdg-13 stubs. Individually they are sub-cm and on axis, and for a 468 MeV shower a tail at 100 cm is physical, so I did not call it over-clustered; if the owner disagrees the movers are exactly those six. NO pi0: no reco group, and kine_pio_* (mass 74.7 from 468.4 + 11.8 at 57.8 deg) is the BDT scan over all candidate pairs, not a pairing -- the 11.8 MeV partner is far below the 20 MeV scope and I did not look at it. 10 of the 11 showers are below the scope threshold and were never drawn. This verdict is about clustering and is silent on PID. Images looked at: 4.

[agent-bulk] Small event, 12 segments, 6 showers, 2 in scope. Verdict shower 18012 (167.2 MeV, pdg 11, 4 seg, 40.2 cm) is the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; the only other in-scope object is 10009 (pdg 13, kine_charge 130.4 / kine_best 105.2), lower on both, so nothing higher was passed over. Vertex judged from the automatic close-in vtxz-* frames (r95 172.1 cm, half_span 215.2, so vtxz fired) plus ov-iso: in vtxz-az-055-el+20 and vtxz-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly at the kink between a grey (unowned) 31 cm proton arm (10001 + 10005, pdg 2212, correctly left unowned) and the orange 41 cm pdg-13 track 10009, at the tip of the vertex charge blob. Clean two-prong vertex, correctly placed -- not a vertex verdict. CORRECT for 18012, with two things the owner should know. First, the geometry: 18012 is FAR detached -- I measured every segment's distance to the main vertex from segments.xs3/ys3/zs3 and its four members sit 158.2-173.8 cm out, with absolutely nothing in between (the next nearest objects to the vertex after cluster 10, which ends at 47 cm, are 38018 at 157.0 cm and 37017 at 160.6 cm, i.e. 18012's own neighbourhood). So this is a 167 MeV EM object 1.6 m from a numucc vertex whose only other visible products are a 31 cm proton and a 41 cm track. Whether it belongs to this neutrino at all is not a clustering question and I am not answering it. Second, the clustering itself is clean: the four members are one contiguous chain (largest internal gap 0.60 cm measured on the member points), 27.3 cm end to end, single apex at the X, and the member set covers the visible point cloud in both shw18012-az-055-el+20 and shw18012-az+085-el+20 -- the two views look very different, the second showing a ~13 cm transverse band of charge that the skeleton does not trace, which is the pilot's skeleton-vs-blob caveat and the reason I did NOT compute any MeV/cm here (correction 18). Membership triple-check: nseg 4 = owner-grouped count 4 = cmp_div's 4. There is no grey/unowned charge anywhere near it -- the event's only unowned segments are the two vertex protons 158 cm away. The one open question is 37017 (23.0 cm, 42.6 deg, 0.6 cm, cluster 37) and 38018 (24.3 cm, 45.3 deg, 0.8 cm, cluster 38): both are 2-point stubs that are seeds of their own sub-20 MeV showers, both sit in 18012's neighbourhood (157-161 cm from the vertex), and at 23-24 cm out and 42-45 deg off axis they are ~16 cm transverse, i.e. ~1.6 Moliere radii -- outside any pass-1 band (they are off the top of the acceptance plot, which shows only the four orange member squares and no non-member circles at all) but not obviously foreign. I have marked BOTH '?' rather than IN: I looked at them and the evidence does not separate 'far tail of the same shower' from 'two independent few-MeV fragments', and their charge is small either way. That is the only reason this is 'likely' rather than 'certain'. NO pi0: no reco group, kine_div has no pairing, and the pio-*.png frames are the auto-slotted top pair (correction 3) -- nothing stored. Showers I did not open frames for: 10009 (I used its table numbers and saw it in the vertex frames as the orange arm) and the 4 sub-scope showers, which were never drawn. This verdict is about clustering and is silent on PID. Images looked at: 6.

[agent-bulk] A clean two-gamma pi0 event, and the reco's pairing survives every check I can make. Verdict shower 59022 (131.0 MeV, pdg 11, 7 seg, 30.2 cm) is the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; the only other in-scope shower is 60030 (96.8 MeV, pdg 11), and there is no higher-energy non-EM object to pass over -- the muon is not a shower here (see below). Vertex judged from the vtx-* sweep at 98.7 cm half-span; r95 is only 79.0 cm so the event never triggered the close-in vtxz-* set and did not need it (correction 20 does not apply to this event). In vtx-az-055-el+20 and vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly at the end of a single 85 cm straight track (segment 11042, pdg 13, UNOWNED/grey -- correctly not swallowed by either shower), with no other prong. CORRECT for 59022: 7 members spanning 0-37.1 cm at 0-10.1 deg, i.e. a tight forward cone that opens and branches, and the member set covers the visible point cloud in shw59022-az-055-el+20. The acceptance plot is all orange squares inside 12.5 deg with no non-member circle at all. Every non-member within 50 cm of its start is BEHIND it: 11042 at 140.4 deg, 48007 at 157.9, 47006 at 117.1, 60030/60031 at 158.9, 53013 at 176.2 -- there is nothing in front to add. Membership triple-check: nseg 7 = owner-grouped count 7 = cmp_div's 7. The event's single grey/unowned segment is the muon 11042, which is where it should be. The other gamma, 60030 (4 seg, 0-24.0 cm at 0-19.2 deg), I judged from its table and the pi0 frame rather than its own zoom frames: same picture, everything within 35 cm of it is at 102-167 deg behind, nseg 4 = owner count 4 = cmp_div 4. PI0 CONFIRMED, and this is the counter-example to the vertex-pi0 pathology I reported in wave 2 and flagged again on evt347824 in this shard. Reco group 0 = 60030 + 59022, stored mass 159.6 MeV. Both gammas are genuinely DETACHED from the neutrino vertex -- I measured the starts against main_vertex: 59022 starts 42.6 cm out, 60030 starts 22.4 cm out -- so the vertex convention has a real chord and BOTH conventions exist and agree: axis convention theta 97.8 deg -> 169.7 MeV, vertex convention theta 90.3 deg -> 159.6 MeV, a 6 percent spread where the disputed events give a factor of two or no number at all. In pio-az-055-el+020 the red and blue gamma diamonds sit on opposite sides of the purple vertex star and each axis arrow points AWAY from it, which is the geometry a real pi0 has to have. I have stored the reco's own pairing to record the agreement. The one number I would not defend is the mass itself: 159.6 MeV is ~18 percent above 135, which is a calibration question (the display also prints the track-hypothesis energies 78.8 and 58.2 MeV for the same charge) and not a clustering one -- I am not adjudicating it. 10 of the 12 showers are below the 20 MeV scope threshold and were never drawn. This verdict is about clustering and is silent on PID. Images looked at: 5.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, 12 segments, 8 showers, only ONE in scope. Verdict shower 13006 (103.8 MeV, pdg 11, 4 seg, 15.9 cm) is the sole in-scope object, so it is trivially the highest-kine_charge pdg-11 shower and nothing was passed over. Vertex judged from the vtx-* sweep at 102.7 cm half-span; r95 is 82.1 cm so the close-in vtxz-* set never fired and was not needed (correction 20 does not apply). In vtx-az-055-el+20 and vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits at the junction of exactly two prongs pointing in roughly OPPOSITE directions: a 65 cm heavily-ionising track (segment 13005, cluster 13, pdg 2212, UNOWNED/grey -- the event's only grey segment) going one way, and the EM object 13006 going the other. Vertex correctly placed. CORRECT for 13006, and the opposite-prong geometry is what makes it correct rather than under-clustered: 13005 is by far the biggest pile of charge in the event and it is grey, which is the classic missing-charge signature, but it is on the OTHER SIDE of the vertex from the shower, so it is not a candidate for membership and leaving it out is right. Membership triple-check: nseg 4 = owner-grouped count 4 = cmp_div's 4. Every non-member near the shower is off-cone: 40010 at 10.4 cm / 84.0 deg, 39009 at 11.4 cm / 129.3 deg, 38008 at 33.6 cm / 40.5 deg, 17007 at 81.8 cm / 78.4 deg -- all 2-point stubs, all off the top of the acceptance plot, which shows only the four orange member squares and no non-member circle. Nothing contiguous and in-cone is missing. The one thing worth the owner's eye is the shower's SHAPE, and I measured it from the member points rather than dividing kine_charge by length (correction 18): the real body is just 13006 + 13004, 28 points spanning 12.5 cm with transverse rms 0.76/0.15 cm -- a compact narrow blob at the vertex -- and the shower's advertised 47.5 cm reach comes entirely from two 0.3 cm, 2-point, pdg-13 stubs, 41011 at 39.8 cm / 9.9 deg and 42012 at 47.5 cm / 21.7 deg, absorbed by pass3_cone across a 27.5 cm gap in which I could find no charge at all (blank in shw13006-az-055-el+20, and no candidate is listed there). I have marked both '?': their charge is negligible so removing them changes no energy, but they are the only reason this object reads as 47 cm rather than 13 cm, and 42012 also sits above the 20.5 deg dashed step on the acceptance plot. I did NOT call over-clustering on them because a 2-point stub picked up on-axis by pass3_cone is the same thing I let stand on evt394167 in this shard, and consistency matters more than a 0.6 cm difference in reach. PID NOT JUDGED, and this is worth stating plainly: a 104 MeV object whose member points span 12.5 cm sits in the ambiguous zone, the reco calls it pdg 11 and the sample calls the event nuecc, and I have neither the granularity nor the calibration to overturn that -- my verdict is about clustering only. NO pi0: no reco group and no second EM object anywhere (the nearest other showers are 2-point stubs at 82, 126, 135 and 158 cm). 7 of the 8 showers are below the 20 MeV scope threshold and were never drawn. Images looked at: 5.

[agent-bulk] Busy multi-prong numucc vertex. Verdict shower 13009 (299.8 MeV, pdg 11, 5 seg, 56.5 cm) = highest-kine_charge pdg-11 object; I passed over TWO higher-kine_charge non-EM objects, 13031 (pdg 13, kine_charge 554.5 / kine_best 678.6, a 341.5 cm muon) and 13030 (pdg 211, kine_charge 114.0 / kine_best 66.6) -- ordering is by kine_charge, per the correction. Vertex judged from the automatic close-in vtxz-* frames (r95 260.5 cm, half_span 325.6, so vtxz fired): in vtxz-az-055-el+20 and vtxz-az+065-el+20 the star sits at a clean convergence of four prongs -- the muon 13031, the pion 13030, an UNOWNED 6.7 cm pdg-2212 stub 13024, and 13009 itself, all of them cluster 13 and all starting at 0.0 cm from the vertex. The vertex is fine; this is not a vertex verdict. OVER-CLUSTERED, unclear, and here is exactly what I saw and what I could not settle. The member set turns through a large angle. In shw13009-az+085-el+20 the yellow set leaves the X at the neutrino vertex, runs ~20 cm, and then KINKS by roughly 60-70 degrees and continues ~25 cm in a new direction; the same direction change shows as a strong bend in shw13009-az-055-el+20, so it is not a projection artefact -- I checked it in two azimuths precisely because a projection can hide or fake a kink. That is the brief's 'the yellow set spans two directions' case. The reason the reconstruction did not see it is worth writing down: the acceptance metric is blind to it. 13025 (27.2 cm, 46 points -- the whole second arm) is listed at 20.9 cm / 2.3 deg and 13011 at 17.0 cm / 3.3 deg, i.e. beautifully on-axis, because the 'angle' column measures the position of a segment's START relative to the axis, and the start of the second arm sits at the kink, which IS on the first arm's axis. An L-shape therefore scores as a perfect cone, and the acceptance plot for this shower is five orange squares with no non-member circle anywhere. Second finding: 13009 absorbed 95059, a 6.5 cm 12-point pdg 2212 segment, at 29.7 cm / 21.7 deg via pass3_cone. I have marked it OUT, and following the pilot's evt175896 lesson I state plainly that this is a PID statement and NOT a geometry one -- at 21.7 deg and 30 cm the pass-1 gate accepted it legitimately. Third, the vertex anchoring: 13009's seed starts at 0.0 cm from the vertex in the same cluster as the muon, the pion and the unowned proton, which is the same pattern I flagged on evt347824 in this shard. I have marked the seed 13009 '?' rather than OUT because the two readings turn on it and I cannot separate them: (a) the reconstruction joined a thin ~17.5 cm vertex TRACK prong to a genuine EM shower that starts ~20 cm out -- the second arm carries the visibly thicker point cloud in shw13009-az+085-el+20, which is what you expect if the shower is the far half; or (b) it is one real ~300 MeV EM object that converted within ~1 cm of the vertex and whose skeleton simply bends, in which case only the 95059 mark stands and the verdict should be 'correct'. Which piece is the intruder depends on which reading is right, so a confident OUT on either end would be a fabricated certainty. That is what 'unclear' is for. One number, offered as an observation and NOT as a PID verdict: I took the extent from the member points (correction 18 -- I did not divide kine_charge by shower_table.length), 99 points spanning 36.6 cm with the largest internal gap 0.6 cm, which puts 299.8 MeV into 36.6 cm; the transverse rms of 4.93/2.02 cm is inflated by the kink itself and I do not trust it as a width. Nothing is missing: every non-member within 25 cm of the start is at 54-172 deg (96066 at 102.3, 76044 at 98.6, 67034 at 76.9, 73040 at 54.4, 69036 at 172.3, 71038 at 78.9), so there is no under-clustering here. Membership triple-check: nseg 5 = owner-grouped count 5 = cmp_div's 5. PI0 CONFIRMED and stored. Reco group 0 = 96066 + 76044, mass 119.5 MeV. Unlike evt347824, this one is healthy: both gammas are detached from the vertex (I measured 96066 at 6.1 cm and 76044 at 10.8 cm), so the vertex convention has a real chord, and the two conventions agree -- axis 153.0 deg -> 126.5 MeV, vertex 133.3 deg -> 119.5 MeV, a 6 percent spread. In pio-az-055-el+020 the red and blue gamma diamonds sit either side of the purple vertex star with their arrows pointing in opposite directions, the back-to-back geometry a low-momentum pi0 must have. The caveat I will name rather than hide: 6 and 11 cm are short conversion distances for two photons at once, and at a vertex that already has a proton, a pion and a muon these two objects could equally be hadronic fragments carrying a pdg-11 label; the mass closing at 119.5/126.5 is the reason I accept the pairing anyway. kine_pio_* names 299.8 + 103.7 at 98.6 deg -> 258.7 MeV, far too heavy, and it is the BDT scan and not a pairing (correction 3) -- I did not read it as one. 11 of the 16 showers are below the 20 MeV scope threshold and were never drawn; of the in-scope five I opened frames only for 13009, using tables and the pi0 frame for 13031, 13030, 76044 and 96066. This verdict is about clustering and, apart from the explicitly-labelled 95059 mark, is silent on PID. Images looked at: 6.
